Theorem B: 4-cycle block supports {a,b},{b,c},{c,d},{d,a} pairwise intersections 1 (adjacent) or 0 (opposite), across blocks 0, block-diagonal J2-free; dependency ra+rc-rb-rd=0 so rank<=3, top-left 3x3 det 1 so exactly 3; total 3*floor(n/4)+(n mod 4)=ceil(3n/4) checked residues 0..3; re-ran construct_upper n=2..12 exact ranks match target. Theorem C: weight<=2 characterization f with no 2-cycles verified (weight-1 rows never cause J2 since size 1; weight-2 pair shares 2 iff equal 2-sets iff 2-cycle); weight-1 case 1+ceil(3(n-1)/4)>=ceil(3n/4) checked residues, C preserves weight<=2; leaf indegree-0 gives column weight 1, C preserves weight<=2 since no one points to leaf; indegree>=1 with sum n forces indegree 1 everywhere so disjoint cycles length>=3 (no fixed points, no 2-cycles), block-diagonal I+P; det(I+P)=1-(-1)^L via lambda^L-1 at -1 gives 2 if L odd (full rank) and 0 if L even with alternating null vector and (L-1)x(L-1) triangular det 1 so rank L-1; L-1>=3L/4 for even L>=4 equality only at 4, L>=3L/4 for odd L; sum >=3n/4 plus integer rounding gives ceil; base n=1 holds. Computationally re-verified weight<=2 exhaustive n=6 valid 28821 min 5, n=7 valid 505876 min 6, n=8 exhaustive 16M valid 10270569 min 6 matching ceil(3n/4). Theorem D: Frobenius rank(G)>= (tr G)^2/||G||_F^2 via Cauchy on eigenvalues, G=MM^T diag w_i off-diag 0/1, denominator Sr+2P=Sr+Sc-W with P=sum C(c_j,2) (each intersecting pair in exactly one column by J2-free) verified; need Sr+Sc<=2W^2/n+W, coarse KST Sr-W<=n(n-1), Sc-W<=n(n-1) gives Sr+Sc<=2W+2n(n-1), suffices W+2n(n-1)<=2W^2/n i.e. 2W^2-Wn-2n^2(n-1)>=0 increasing in W (4W-n>0), minimal W=3n gives n^2(17-2n)>=0 true for n<=8 (n=8 gives 64>0); light row/column peeling ratios 1+ceil((n-1)/2)>=ceil(n/2) and 1+ceil((n-2)/2)>=ceil(n/2) checked even/odd; n=6 all>=3 impossible via 6n>n(n-1); sequential induction 6 then 7 then 8 valid. No overclaim: general n/2 only to n<=8, full 3n/4 as Conjecture E with heuristic support, clearly separated. One non-decisive presentation defect: minors_n5.csv writes canonical rep c but minor rows/cols/det for different member M in same orbit (export_csv.py lines 119-120), so literal check of minor on displayed rep fails (e.g. orbit 19 det 2 vs 1 on rep; orbit 98 minor singular on rep). Underlying existence claim is TRUE by independent per-matrix check (bad=0), and hand induction already proves r5>=4 without CSV, so defect does not falsify any theorem; corrected in RESULT artifacts.

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison, not timestamp. Fetched and compared three nearest sources. (1) arXiv:2206.04089 Kovacs On Minimally Non-Firm Binary Matrices: studies Boolean rank br(X) vs isolation number i(X) (max 1s with no two sharing row/column/J2) and firm/superfirm equality for all submatrices, four infinite minimally-non-firm classes via rectangle-cover graph. Same J2 configuration but different rank notion (Boolean vs real) and different question (equality vs minimum real rank under diagonal-ones normalization); its infinite families do not give real-rank minima. (2) arXiv:1806.00638 Haviv On Minrank and Forbidden Subgraphs: minrank over fits (diagonal nonzero, zeros on nonedges, entries free) maximized over graphs with H-free complement, Omega(sqrt(n)/log n) and n^delta bounds. Our rank is of the 0-1 matrix itself, diagonal fixed to 1 not just nonzero, forbidden pattern is constant all-ones 2x2 anywhere, minimization over matrices not maximization over graphs; bounds do not imply small-n exact minima. (3) arXiv:2507.05824 Parnas-Shraibman Binary/Boolean rank with small constant real rank d<=4: fixes real rank and bounds binary/Boolean rank above it with tight gaps and extremal circulants plus computer search. Our direction orthogonal: fix J2-free plus diagonal-ones, minimize real rank itself, seek exact r(n) and ceil(3n/4) tiling; their d<=4 classification does not contain diagonal-ones J2-free minima (our n=5 minimizers have real rank 4 but extremal for different property). arXiv search for 'no all-ones 2x2 rank' returned no results, supporting absence of same-objective study. No prior source found studies minimum real (rational) rank over diagonal-ones J2-free matrices, exact table r(2..5)=2,3,3,4 with 6/390 minimizer classification, or 4-cycle tiling upper bound with weight<=2 optimality; delta is (i) real rank as objective, (ii) diagonal-ones normalization making minimum nontrivial, (iii) exact-minimum plus tiling bound. Not parameter substitution of known theorems; methods stay in combinatorial linear algebra (peeling, functional digraphs, Frobenius+KST) as claimed.

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later, not textbook/parameter/tiny-gain/unexplained enumeration. Defines new natural extremal problem (C4-free bipartite condition plus diagonal-ones normalization; without normalization zero matrix trivializes) linking forbidden-pattern combinatorics to rank rigidity/minrank/biclique-cover context. Provides first exact values r(2)=2,r(3)=3,r(4)=3,r(5)=4 with human-checkable inductions plus machine certificates (counts, 1 and 5 minimizer orbits, 107 survivor orbits, explicit nonsingular minors) - explained catalog, not raw table: weight-multisets, canonical forms, J2/rank verification. Provides general theorems for all n: ceil(3n/4) upper bound by explicit 4-cycle block-diagonal tiling (non-obvious 3/4 ratio emerging from 4-cycles) and matching lower bound proving tiling optimal among all row-weight<=2 matrices via leaf+cycle induction - infinite-family result, not just small n. Extends general lower bound ceil(n/2) to n<=8 via peeling+Frobenius+KST with honest open step for n>=9 all>=3 and sharp conjecture r(n)=ceil(3n/4) supported by exhaustive weight<=2 to n=8 and heuristic to n=12, clearly separating theorem vs conjecture. Small-n table plus sharp tiling plus sparse optimality plus conjecture forms coherent reference point for future C4-free rank work; rediscovery would merit recording. Rejects textbook restatement (no textbook contains this table/bound), mere substitution (new objective/normalization), tiny gain (3/4 vs 1/2 gap is substantive, sparse optimality is tight), unexplained enumeration (grouped orbits+minors+hand proofs).
